question: Can a neural network's parameters be decomposed directly into faithful, sparsely used, simple components that recover ground-truth mechanisms in superposition and across layers?

key_findings.claim: Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition defines mechanisms as additive parameter-space vectors optimized for faithfulness, per-input minimality, and low-rank/layer simplicity.
key_findings.evidence: The sum of components matches the target parameters; gradient attributions select a batch top-k subset whose forward pass matches target behavior; Schatten-p penalties encourage simple component matrices.

key_findings.claim: APD recovers individual feature mechanisms in the canonical toy model of superposition.
key_findings.evidence: Learned parameter components align with the target weight columns at mean-max cosine similarity near one in 5-to-2 and 40-to-10 settings, although component magnitudes shrink to roughly 0.9 of target columns.

key_findings.claim: Parameter components separate more nonlinear functions than there are neurons and can span multiple layers.
key_findings.evidence: Compressed-computation toys assign individual computations to recovered components despite a narrow hidden layer, and the cross-layer experiment recovers components whose matrices jointly implement distributed mechanisms across two layers.

key_findings.claim: The current method is computationally expensive, brittle to hyperparameters, and dependent on approximate gradient attribution.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion limits APD to toy models, notes worst-case memory/cost approaching quadratic in target parameter count, reports extensive tuning, and identifies saturation failures of first-order attributions.

key_findings.claim: APD is not fully invariant to function-preserving parameterization because its simplicity penalty privileges layer boundaries and matrix rank.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.2.4 acknowledges that the same computation spread across layers may receive a larger simplicity cost than a one-layer implementation, so decomposition can reflect architecture as well as algorithm.

key_findings.claim: The proposed feature definition—inputs that activate a minimal mechanism—is conceptually useful but not yet shown unique or human-interpretable in realistic models.
key_findings.evidence: The paper argues MDL components avoid arbitrary feature splitting, yet multiple decompositions can trade faithfulness, top-k usage, and Schatten simplicity; all validation uses synthetic ground truth.

method.core_idea: Learn an additive decomposition of a fixed network's parameters whose components form a short mechanistic description of its input-dependent computation.
method.mechanism: Optimize component sums to reconstruct weights, attribute outputs to components, execute only the most attributed subset per batch, match the original model's outputs/selected hidden states, and penalize component rank via Schatten quasi-norms.
assumptions: Underlying mechanisms combine approximately additively in parameter space.
Sparse per-input component use is a useful proxy for mechanistic minimality.
Low matrix rank and limited layer span are useful proxies for simplicity.
Gradient attribution ranks causal component importance accurately enough during training.
The chosen loss weights, component count, and batch top-k expose rather than invent the mechanism decomposition.

techniques.role: Represents the target parameter vector as a sum of mechanism components.
Ranks which components matter for each batch output.
Forces a sparse set of components to reproduce target behavior.
Combines faithfulness, minimality, and simplicity as the selection principle.

evaluations.setting: Toy model of superposition with 5/2 and 40/10 input/hidden dimensions.
evaluations.metric: Mean maximum cosine similarity and mean L2 magnitude ratio to ground-truth weight-column mechanisms.
evaluations.result: Direction recovery is near perfect; magnitudes exhibit about ten-percent shrinkage and the smallest setting is brittle.

evaluations.setting: Compressed nonlinear computation with more functions than hidden neurons.
evaluations.metric: Alignment of learned components with ground-truth per-function parameter paths and sparse reconstruction.
evaluations.result: APD separates individual computations despite superposition in the bottleneck.
evaluations.baseline: Neuron-aligned decomposition, which cannot allocate one neuron per function.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer compressed computation with cross-layer distributed representations.
evaluations.metric: Recovery of ground-truth function components across matrices and output fidelity.
evaluations.result: Learned components span layers and correspond to individual mechanisms in the toy construction.

limitations: All demonstrated successes use small toys with known mechanisms.
Memory and compute can scale prohibitively with parameter count times component count.
Gradient attributions can fail under saturation or nonlinear component interactions.
Bias parameters are not decomposed in the current implementation.
Rank-based simplicity is not invariant to mixing computations across layers.
The objective does not prove uniqueness of the resulting decomposition.
failure_modes: Components shrink or mix mechanisms to balance minimality against rank penalty.
Batch top-k can force an incorrect fixed sparsity pattern across heterogeneous examples.
First-order attributions can miss causally important saturated paths.
Non-additive interactions can require combinations that no individual parameter vector captures cleanly.
Excess component capacity or loss-weight changes can yield alternative decompositions.
Cross-layer mechanisms can be over-penalized relative to architecturally local ones.
reusable_insights: Define interpretability components by fidelity to the original parameters as well as activations.
Separate a mechanism's representation from the inputs or features that activate it.
Use known-mechanism toys to audit decomposition objectives before scaling.
Description-length objectives make assumptions about simplicity explicit and testable.
open_questions: Can low-rank factorized components reduce APD cost enough for language models?
Which causal attribution estimator is accurate and affordable during decomposition training?
Can simplicity be defined invariantly under layer-mixing reparameterizations?
How stable are components across seeds, loss weights, top-k values, and component counts?
Do APD components support reliable editing, anomaly detection, or unlearning in real models?

competitive_landscape.title: Toy Models of Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Elhage et al. characterize activation-direction superposition; APD uses its toy as a test and decomposes the corresponding parameters into per-feature mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: SAEs scale sparse feature discovery to language models but introduce reconstruction and feature-splitting issues; APD targets parameter mechanisms and cross-layer computation, currently only in toys.

competitive_landscape.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
competitive_landscape.difference: Transcoders replace dense MLP transformations with sparse learned features at up to 1.4B scale; APD decomposes original parameters additively and can in principle span layers without a replacement network.

competitive_landscape.title: AtP*: An efficient and scalable method for localizing LLM behaviour to components
competitive_landscape.difference: AtP* audits and improves gradient approximations for component localization in LLMs; APD uses simpler gradient attribution inside a generative decomposition objective and identifies attribution robustness as unfinished work.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: APD inaugurates parameter-first interpretability by recovering minimal mechanisms in superposition, compressed computation, and cross-layer distributed representations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Three ground-truth toy families show high alignment between learned and intended components under a unified MDL-inspired objective.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The parameter-space objective and cross-layer mechanism target are distinctive. Claims about architecture-agnostic feature foundations remain prospective until APD becomes stable, identifiable, and scalable beyond synthetic networks.
